title: WALES MILLENNIUM CENTRE TOURS (ENGLISH)
description:
Take our backstage tour and get an exclusive behind-the-scenes glimpse into the world of theatre.

Beginning at our iconic Donald Gordon Theatre, you’ll be guided through our rarely seen backstage areas before ending your tour with an opportunity for photos by our famous inscription wall.

Afterwards, take your time to explore our front of house spaces, architecture and art, grab a seat and watch the world go by from our ground floor café-bar, Ffwrnais. Your delicious lunch, coffee or fresh pastry will taste all the better knowing you get 10% off by showing your tour ticket. You can also visit Armadilo, our theatre Shop, where you’ll also enjoy 10% off with your ticket—perfect for picking up a unique gift or souvenir.

We pride ourselves on being open and welcoming to everyone. If you have any specific access requirements, please contact us before the tour so that we can make any necessary arrangements.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Wales Millennium Centre Tours (English)

title: JIVE ACES
description:
Got the blues? Well, step right up, because The Jive Aces are bringing their swingin' show to town, and it’s gonna' flip your frown upside down! When these cats burst onto the stage in their signature yellow suits, you’ll be tapping your feet and grinning like a fool before you know it. This is more than just a show, it’s a proper good time packed with the hottest music from sizzling swing to the raucous roots of rock 'n' roll, that’ll leave you buzzing.

For 30 years they've have been taking their infectious tunes to over 40 countries and continuously proving why they are the UK’s No.1 jive and swing band. They effortlessly transition from smooth-as-butter ballads to rip-roaring rhythm & blues. They’ve played for the Queen, packed out the Royal Albert Hall, and made history as the first band to get to the Britain’s Got Talent finals. With 250 gigs a year, they’ve got a knack for turning any crowd into a dancing, cheering frenzy

You’ve probably caught their rendition of the Morecambe and Wise classic "Bring Me Sunshine" - a banger with nearly 4 million YouTube views that’s so upbeat a U.S. doctor prescribed it to chase away the blues. It’s been all over Strictly Come Dancing, Netflix, an American cop show and recently comedian Miranda Hart even declared it one of her favourite songs and stated on BBC Radio 3, "The Jive Aces will get me up off the floor and make me lose any self-consciousness and dance!

Their latest album, Keeping The Show On The Road, is stuffed with crowd favourites that hit No.1 on Mike Read’s Heritage Chart and got spins on BBC and Boom Radio. Those tracks, plus their classic hits, will have you moving from the first note.

These guys and gals are the real deal. They’ve shared stages with legends like Van Morrison, John Travolta, Priscilla Presley, Jamie Cullum, Toto and Status Quo, and nabbed awards like the City of Derry International Music Award and the Variety Club of Great Britain Award for their music and charity work. Their music videos? So sharp they’ve won film festival prizes. But what makes The Jive Aces special is how they make you feel like you’re right in the heart of the party.

Don’t miss the "Feelin’ Happy" Tour! Grab your dancing shoes and get ready for a night of swing, jive, and pure, unfiltered entertainment that’ll send you home with more uplifted than a hot air balloon race. Snag your tickets now for a show that’ll keep you smiling for days!
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Jive Aces

title: GALLIFREY CABARET
description:
The queerest TARDIS in space and time!

Hop aboard GALLIFREY CABARET for a spectacular night of cosmic drag and variety, all inspired by the greatest TV show in the universe – DOCTOR WHO!

This cult hit is coming to Cardiff. Featuring drag, stand-up, burlesque, music, and a vortex of other surprises, this huge cabaret celebrates being queer in the wild, mad, and wonderful Whoniverse.

The show is bold, inclusive, joyful, punk, and unapologetically queer – we’re committed to showcasing a broad and inclusive range of artists and performances.

The shows are hosted by Reece Connolly as the Doctor, with performances by Carrot (usually appearing as Donna Noble in drag) and special guest performers, all bringing characters from the Whoniverse to life.

Since our first show in November 2021, we’ve performed regularly at the Royal Vauxhall Tavern in London, and more recently moved to a new home at The Clapham Grand. The show has toured across the UK, including Cardiff, Brighton, and Manchester.

Please note: this is an unofficial tribute show and is not affiliated with the BBC or any other large, scary corporations.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Gallifrey Cabaret

title: IN MEMORY OF AMY
description:
Anna Aarons' dedicated show in memory of the late, great Amy Winehouse celebrates its 10 year anniversary this year, as well as commemorating 15 years since the legend's passing.

Not a 'typical' tribute, Aarons', joined by her 5 piece band, takes audiences on a thoughtful journey of Winehouse's catalogue, her musical influences, as well as sewing in her original music; portraying Winehouse's influence on modern songwriting. After multiple sold out shows across Central London, Aarons is delighted to bring this highly regarded show to the Cabaret Millenium Centre.

Vocals - Anna AaronsKeys - Gareth BucklandGuitar - Magnus EricsonBass - Mehmet RaifDrums - Will JacksonSax - Kerry Williams

title: FACILITATOR TRAINING
description:
Are you aged 18–30 and interested in running your own workshops?

Whether you’re already involved in creative projects or looking to take the first step, this is your chance to build the skills you need to become a confident, engaging facilitator – and open up new employment opportunities along the way.

Over 10 weekly sessions, you’ll get an overview of what it takes to plan and deliver brilliant workshops – especially for young audiences. Together we’ll:

The sessions will be led by experienced facilitators and theatre-makers, Flossy and Boo, and we’ll also be inviting in seasoned facilitators and workshop leaders from across the creative sector to provide their insight and experience.

There’ll also be an opportunity to attend a development workshop with the Royal Shakespeare Company.

Following the completion of the course, you will be offered short-term placements with Youth Arts organisations across South Wales – a unique opportunity to help develop your skills and CV.

Thursdays, 17 September – 26 November (no session 29 October)

6pm – 8.30pm

Platfform, Wales Millennium Centre

This is a free opportunity you won’t find anywhere else – a chance to learn, connect, and grow your confidence without spending a penny.  Whether you want to add to your CV, open up more paid opportunities, or simply try something new, you’ll leave with skills you can use across the creative sector and beyond.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Facilitator Training

title: TOM WARD
description:
Before Tom bails out on the modern world entirely to commit to nostalgia full-time, the burner phone using, Discman carrying, 1988-1995 obsessed freak is giving the present tense one last try. Not for him, but for his 2-year-old son who lives there. But how does 2026 compare to the one he grew up in? Tom explores the head f**k of popular culture in the modern world versus that of his youth in his trademark bittersweet style.

As seen on Live at the Apollo, Roast Battle and Qi.

title: WELSH NATIONAL OPERA: BLUEBEARD’S CASTLE + OEDIPUS REX
description:
In this powerful double bill, two extraordinary works of the 20th century are brought together in a shared world of ritual, mystery and psychological intensity.

In Bluebeard’s Castle, Judith leaves everything behind to be with the enigmatic Duke Bluebeard. She soon discovers his home is filled with locked doors and as she demands each one be opened, she uncovers not only the secrets of his past, but something far more unsettling. As darkness gathers, love and fear become impossible to separate.

In the second half, the same stark setting becomes the ancient city of Thebes for Oedipus Rex. A plague grips the land, and its king is determined to uncover the truth behind it. As his search intensifies, he is forced to confront a destiny he cannot escape. What begins as a quest for answers, becomes a devastating revelation.

Gothic, atmospheric and visually striking, this unified staging draws powerful connections between two timeless myths.

Featuring music by Hildegard Von Bingen Conductor Lidiya Yankovskaya Director Joe Hill-Gibbins

Cast Nathan Berg, Peter Hoare, Christine Rice

Original production of Bluebeard’s Castle English National Opera
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Welsh National Opera: Bluebeard’s Castle + Oedipus Rex

Expect surreal stories, sharp observations and the sort of comedy that makes you laugh first and ask “wait, what just happened?” later.

title: OPEN OFFICE
description:
Are you a Theatre or Cabaret Artist looking to connect with Wales Millennium Centre?

Open Office is your opportunity to chat with us! We are mixing things up a little this year and giving you access to our Productions Producers and Cabaret Producer.

Victoria John - Senior Producer for Productions and Lauren Hughes - Assistant Producer for Productions

This is a chance for you to come and meet V and Lauren, chat about an idea, get advice or find out more about our Artist Development programme and creative opportunities.

This will be an informal chat over coffee in a relaxed environment. V and Lauren are keen to meet as many Theatre Artists as possible, to find out more about you and your practice, so come along!

Sessions with V and Lauren are: 28th August, 30th October and 27th November 2026 at 10am, 11.30am, 1.30pm or 3pm

Aled Lloyd Rees - Cabaret Producer

Do you have an idea for a cabaret show? Are you looking for advice or interested in developing work in cabaret?

Aled Lloyd Rees is hosting informal conversations as an opportunity to share ideas, ask questions and explore how your work could develop, all in a relaxed setting over a coffee.

Whether you are an emerging artist or already creating work, Aled is keen to connect, listen and support the growth of cabaret in Wales. Sessions with Aled are 7th August and 25th September 2026 at 10am, 11.30am, 1.30pm or 3pm.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Open Office

Prepare to be dazzled by Trisha McCluney, star of BBC1’s “I Can See Your Voice” and one of the fastest-rising tribute artists.

As Essentially Cher, Trisha brings the magic of the legendary Cher to life, delivering a breathtakingly authentic experience.

Fresh off the back of her Australian tour with Las Vegas show "Legends in Concert", Trisha is coming to the Wales Millennium Centre on Fri 25th Sept to deliver her World class tribute to the Goddess of Pop. Trisha's ability to deliver every nuance of Cher's presence, from her striking resemblance to her powerful vocals and not forgetting her signature wit and sass is so flawlessly accurate that audiences consistently say it feels as though they are watching the real thing!This must-see show features an electrifying setlist of Cher’s greatest hits, including:

title: PROTEST, POWER, REVOLUTION, RESISTANCE
description:
Protest, Power, Revolution, Resistance is a concert with something urgent to say.

Conducted by Johanna Malangré, current Music Director of the Orchestre de Picardie in France, the programme showcases her electrifying musicality and imaginative leadership.

It begins with Joan Tower’s Fanfare for the Uncommon Woman, a brilliant, bracing piece for brass and percussion inspired by Copland’s famous fanfare but reimagined as a celebration of women who lead, risk, and transform the world. From there, the orchestra moves into the powerful sound world of Margaret Bonds’ The Montgomery Variations, written in response to the civil rights movement and shaped by Bonds’ experience of Montgomery, Alabama. Both reflective and resolute, its movements capture the collective determination of protest and the sense of a new beginning.

After the interval, Haydn’s Farewell Symphony reminds us that messages in music are not always shouted, sometimes they are staged with quiet ingenuity. What begins as a tense, impassioned symphony becomes a theatrical plea for compassion, as players famously leave the stage one by one. Finally, Shostakovich’s Ninth Symphony turns expectations upside down. Written in 1945, when a monumental victory symphony was demanded, Shostakovich produced instead a compact, spirited, and unpredictably shadowed work.

REFLECTIVE · COURAGEOUS · IMAGINATIVE

Joan Tower Fanfare for the Uncommon Woman Bonds The Montgomery Variations Haydn Symphony No.45 (Farewell Symphony) Interval Shostakovich Symphony No.9
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Protest, Power, Revolution, Resistance

title: WALES MILLENNIUM CENTRE TOURS (WELSH)
description:
Take our backstage tour and get an exclusive behind-the-scenes glimpse into the world of theatre.

Beginning at our iconic Donald Gordon Theatre, you’ll be guided through our rarely seen backstage areas before ending your tour with an opportunity for photos by our famous inscription wall.

Afterwards, take your time to explore our front of house spaces, architecture and art, grab a seat and watch the world go by from our ground floor café-bar, Ffwrnais. Your delicious lunch, coffee or fresh pastry will taste all the better knowing you get 10% off by showing your tour ticket. You can also visit Armadilo, our theatre Shop, where you’ll also enjoy 10% off with your ticket—perfect for picking up a unique gift or souvenir.

We pride ourselves on being open and welcoming to everyone. If you have any specific access requirements, please contact us before the tour so that we can make any necessary arrangements.

title: WELSH NATIONAL OPERA: LA BOHÈME
description:
In the Latin Quarter of Paris, four young artists live for the moment, sharing what little they have; chasing big dreams and laughing through the cold.

When Rodolfo meets Mimì, a quiet seamstress with a fading light, their connection is instant and unforgettable. But in a world shaped by poverty and passion, love burns brightly but all too briefly.

Puccini’s deeply moving masterpiece captures the passion of youth through some of the most beautiful and recognisable music ever written. La bohème evokes the spirit and intensity of bohemian life: the joy of falling in love, the pain of letting go, and the fragile of it all.

This acclaimed production reimagines this beloved story with striking clarity and emotional power. Set in a stark, monochrome world inspired by 1930s Paris where shadows linger and the presence of death is never far away.

The result is a La bohème that feels both timeless and contemporary. It paints a vivid portrait of young lives lived on the edge, where every moment matters and every goodbye cuts deep.

wno.org.uk/boheme

Original production Glyndebourne

Conductor Corinna NiemeyerDirector Floris Visser

Rodolfo Carlos Cardoso

Mimì Alexia Voulgaridou

title: THE ART OF CHANGE | BODIES OF WATER | ÔL HAUNTS
description:
Welcome to Wales Millennium Centre's first VR Cinema (daytime programme) - an exciting opportunity for audiences to experience 3 extraordinary virtual reality works back to back.

The Art of Change is a deeply personal audio-visual journey that traverses time and space. Using a “feedback loop” of recorded voice memos addressed to past and future selves, it maps pivotal moments on a multi-sensory life map.

The project interweaves tape-recorded messages from various life stages within the music, narrating a woman’s story as she communicates with herself across time. The journey unfolds through past, present, and future, depicting archetypal experiences familiar to many: the majestic solitude of a large tree in the wilderness, the challenge of an insurmountable mountain peak, the mundanity of an ordinary office building, and the yearning to escape, along with more abstract, imaginary places.

The Art of Change reflects on life’s steps and their echo across time and space. Entirely painted and animated in VR using Quill, it offers a pioneering musical journey. Through virtual space, seamless transitions, and increasingly complex environments, this immersive project redefines how we appreciate music.

The VR film BODIES OF WATER invites you to hold your breath and let yourself be transported and transformed by water in the company of curious individuals. As night falls, they invade a public swimming pool. These bodies of water, immersed in the watery mass, transgress the limits of their natural environment and metamorphose. They then engage in a contemporary dance that reveals them differently. The aquatic environment makes them supple and light, but also vulnerable and combative. This poetic mass, encompassing and suffocating, unites, separates and constitutes them. BODIES OF WATER explores the transformation of human bodies as they interact with water - a fluid and adaptable medium that simultaneously presents resistance. It takes you underwater for an immersive experience that unfolds an uncommon and otherwise inaccessible contemporary dance.

It’s 2006. In a small town in North Wales, 16-year-old Morgan stands on the edge of his future, guiding us through haunts, hangouts and nights that linger long after the last bus leaves.

The year is 2006, Tony Blair is Prime Minister, Twitter has just been launched, and young people are quickly getting used to a world where social media and technology are beginning to take hold. 16-year-old Morgan, voiced by Callum Scott Howells (It’s a Sin) and Steffan Donnelly (Theatr Cymru), is searching to understand where he belongs, his journey set against the backdrop of a community in Llanberis - a small town at the foot of Snowdon in Wales.

Directed by Tomos Chetwode-Barton and Lucy Hammond (Monoliths, Traitor) with immersive concept development by Dreaming Methods, we are transported to a time when analog and digital worlds collide, sharing moments from Morgan’s life as he travels through this poetic rite-of-passage odyssey.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > The Art of Change | Bodies of Water | Ôl Haunts

title: WELSH NATIONAL OPERA: SCHOOLS CONCERT
description:
Welsh National Opera’s Schools Concert is back with a vibrant and welcoming introduction to live orchestral music for pupils from years three to seven.

With a theme of Roman and Greek mythology, hosted by Elin Llwyd, this free concert blends well-known hits with rarer pieces, all brought to life by WNO Orchestra and a group of outstanding soloists. Offenbach’s energetic Can-Can brings a sense of joy and familiarity, encouraging young audiences to connect straight away. Meanwhile, Beethoven’s music from Prometheus stands out with its bold, cinematic quality – almost like a superhero soundtrack – making it both accessible and thrilling, even for those new to classical music.

Adding to the playful atmosphere is Ballo de Orsi (‘Dance of the Bears’), a piece that feels wonderfully visual and full of character. Its lively narrative quality invites children to imagine scenes and movement, making the listening experience fun and immersive.

With its mythological theme, engaging repertoire and relaxed setting, this concert aims to create a memorable experience for the children attending, encouraging a passion for music and creativity.

The concert is designed to support the Curriculum for Wales and National Curriculum in England and is augmented by a free resource pack for teachers to support classroom learning before and after the event.

The concerts in Cardiff and Llandudno will be presented in the Welsh language.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Welsh National Opera: Schools Concert

title: WELSH NATIONAL OPERA: FAMILY CONCERT
description:

Adding to the playful atmosphere is Ballo de Orsi (‘Dance of the Bears’), a piece that feels wonderfully visual and full of character. Its lively, almost storytelling quality, invites children to imagine scenes and movement, making the listening experience both fun and immersive.

With its mythological theme, engaging repertoire and relaxed setting, this concert offers something enjoyable and memorable for everyone.

title: JUST FOR YOU TRILOGY
description:
Welcome to Wales Millennium Centre's first VR Cinema (evening programme) - an exciting opportunity for audiences to experience Craig Quintero's extraordinary Just for You Trilogy, 3 virtual reality shortfilms played back to back.

We are comforted by facts, by the familiarity of things we know to be “true.” The sun rises in the east. There are twenty-four hours in a day. I exist. These truisms simplify our lives, enable us to get through the process of living. We are not afraid to leap into the air, because we know we will land on the ground. The Just for You Trilogy explores the possibilities that exist beyond these everyday patterns, that blur the lines between dream and reality.

Combining Riverbed’s three award-winning 360VR films (All That Remains, Over the Rainbow, and A Simple Silence) into a single experience, the Just for You Trilogy immerses the audience in a surreal meditation on memory, death, and desire.

Presented as part of our VR Cinema programming, this trilogy by Craig Quintero also marks the return of a creator we previously spotlighted during PHI’s Taiwan showcase in 2022.

In "Just for You," Craig Quintero masterfully brings his theatrical expertise into the immersive medium. The audience can feel the precision of stagecraft in every frame, the emotional depth of the characters, and an unsettling closeness with the protagonists. This trilogy creates a rare and powerful connection between viewer and subject—between what is seen and what is felt.

Despite all of our knowing, we will never be known. All That Remains is a meditation on the fluid boundary between dream and reality, fear and desire. It is an invitation to see and be seen.

Forgoing a linear narrative, Over the Rainbow immerses the audience in a surreal landscape. The experience, like life, does not have a singular plot or meaning. Something happens, and then something else happens. Instead of providing a clear-cut moral message, Over the Rainbow encourages the audience to engage the sensations of the moment and embrace the uncertainty of the unknown.

A Simple Silence is the final chapter in Riverbed Theatre’s award-winning Just For You Trilogy . This 360VR experience continues the series’ exploration of our connectedness to the world around us, imbuing the environment with an animistic quality while also blurring the boundary between seeing and being seen. The audience is not a witness to the experience; they are the experience.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Just for You Trilogy

title: HANNAH HORTON
description:
Stories on the Wind is the new live show from award winning saxophonist, composer and Selmer Artist Hannah Horton.

Named by Jazzwise as one to watch in 2026, Hannah brings her deeply personal new album to the stage with a quartet built on lyrical melody, groove, warmth and musical storytelling.

The show moves between intimate reflection and rhythmic energy, with Hannah’s distinctive sound on tenor and baritone saxophones at its heart. This is music shaped by memory, connection, hope and the quiet stories that stay with us. Spacious, melodic and deeply human, Stories on the Wind invites audiences into Hannah’s most personal musical world yet.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > HANNAH HORTON

title: AUDREY HEARTBURN AND MOODY JUDY:
description:
Award-winning musical comedian Tracey Collins returns with a bold double bill, reimagining Hollywood icons Audrey Hepburn and Judy Garland through music, comedy, and theatrical reinvention.

Audrey Heartburn:The evening opens in joyful chaos with Audrey Heartburn. Audrey has left the heartbreak of Hollywood behind and arrived in Soho for a boogie-woogie and a drinky- winky. Expect audience play, spontaneous song, and shared snacks!

Moody Judy:The evening closes with Moody Judy. In this comedic reimagining, Judy Garland discovers The Smiths and recognises her own story in their Manchester melancholy. These cult classics become cabaret confessions with a splash of razzle-dazzle and with high leg kicks.

There Is a Spotlight That Never Goes Out is an intimate, original evening of musical comedy not to be missed.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Audrey Heartburn and Moody Judy:

title: MICHAEL AKADIRI: DON’T CALL ME UNCLE!
description:
Following two hit UK tours, Biggest Award in Comedy nominee and resident (junior) Doctor Michael Akadiri prescribes Cardiff with a potent dose of his latest offering, Don’t Call Me Uncle!

Multi-award-winning comedian Michael is proud to wear many hats: doctor, husband & father. Evidently, that list does not include uncle.

Yet, despite only being in his early 30s, “the supremely talented and likeable” (Metro) doctor, for the first time ever, was recently called uncle in public (a term usually reserved for elders!). This has sent him spiralling!

Join the ”‘hugely entertaining” (Chortle) Akadiri as he fights this lurid allegation, contemplates the difference between perception and reality all whilst keeping the laughs flowing with his trademark “sharp-wit” (Chortle) & “politically punchy” (Guardian) anecdotes.

As seen on Comedy Central LIVE, ITVs Stand Up Sketch & Channel 4’s Stand Up to Cancer. As heard on Capital Xtra’s Breakfast Show, LBC & BBC Radio 4’s Loose Ends Tour support for Jason Manford.

Winner - Komedia New Comedy AwardWinner - Comedian of Medicine Award, Haags Comedy FestivalNextUp Biggest Award in Comedy nominee
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Michael Akadiri: Don’t Call Me Uncle!

title: KATHERINE JENKINS 25 YEAR ANNIVERSARY TOUR
description:
The biggest selling classical artist of this century, Katherine Jenkins OBE, has today announced a brand new 18-date UK tour for 2026, to celebrate her incredible 25 Years in music.

The 25 Year Anniversary Tour is the first tour for Katherine in five years and is set to feature all her biggest hits including ‘Time To Say Goodbye’, the emotional ‘Jealous of the Angels’ and  ‘I Will Always Love You' and more.

Speaking on what it means to celebrate 25 years, Katherine says: “Reaching twenty-five years in music is incredibly emotional, but this tour is truly a celebration of the fans who have been there from the very beginning. To be heading out across the UK and Ireland for eighteen special shows feels less like a celebration of a career and more like a reunion with old friends and I can’t wait to stand on stage, look out into those familiar faces, and share it all over again.”

Katherine Jenkins OBE is officially the world’s most successful classical singer, having been named The Biggest Selling Classical Artist of the Century by Classic FM and earning a record-breaking 14 number-one albums since signing to Universal Classics at just 22. She burst onto the music scene in 2003 with a landmark performance at Westminster Cathedral honouring Pope John Paul II, followed by appearances at major international sporting events and at the Sydney Opera House.

A favourite of the British Royal Family, Jenkins has sung at many national occasions including Her Majesty Queen Elizabeth II’s Diamond Jubilee, Coronation concerts at Buckingham Palace, and her 90th birthday celebrations at Windsor Castle. She has also performed for Popes, Presidents and Princes, further establishing her place as one of the world’s most in-demand classical performers.

Alongside her musical achievements, Katherine has earned ‘National Treasure” status through her charitable work. She serves as global patron of The Wilderness Foundation, ambassador for Prince William’s TUSK Trust and Macmillan Cancer Support, and trustee of The British Forces Foundation - for whom she has performed for troops in conflict zones around the world. Awarded an OBE in 2013, she also lifted spirits during the 2020 pandemic with 25 free “lockdown live” concerts, including history-making performances at Buckingham Palace and a behind-closed-doors Royal Albert Hall concert.

A versatile creative force, Katherine has performed and recorded with many of the world’s leading artists, made her West End debut in Carousel to critical acclaim, and earned television recognition with appearances in Doctor Who, Dancing with the Stars (runner-up), and as a presenter on Songs of Praise. Her recent ventures include roles in films Minamata and Dream Horse, becoming Lady Sponsor of HMS Cardiff, launching her award-winning luxury gin brand Cygnet, and opening the inaugural SXSW London festival.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Katherine Jenkins 25 Year Anniversary Tour

title: SHOVEL DANCE COLLECTIVE + NAIMA BOCK
description:
Join us in the Weston Studio for an evening of captivating music from two incredible artists.

Shovel Dance Collective are a group of nine musicians united by a passion for the beauty, force, and political charge of the traditional musics of Britain, Ireland and beyond. They are committed to Folk music not as an archaeological artifact to be unearthed, but as a living communal activity - inviting and generous to those it speaks to. They arrange the source material into a kind of musique boue (mud music), simultaneously traditional and experimental they engage a deep, cross-temporal synthesis of free improvisation, tape manipulation and field recordings. Their music appears as a patchwork as pieces are stitched together, rearranged and recontextualised. The yarn is threaded with their sense of aesthetic innovation, and with a deep sense of the ways in which traditional music holds the voices of the oppressed and those who, by their labour, create the wealth of the world.

They have performed sold out shows across the UK, with headline concerts at venues such as Cafe OTO, Kings Place and Cecil Sharp House. The collective have appeared at many major festivals: Glastonbury, Roskilde, SXSW, Rewire, Green Man, End of the Road, Sidmouth Folk Festival, Supernormal and Supersonic festivals among others. Publications such as The Wire, Loud and Quiet, NME, Financial Times and The Times have heralded their live performances across the years. Their albums ‘The Shovel Dance’ and ‘The Water is the Shovel of the Shore’ have been championed by The Wire, MOJO, Uncut, KLOF, Songlines et al. and both were named albums of the year by The Quietus.

Most of the writing of Naima Bock’s second album, Below A Massive Dark Land (out 27 September via Sub Pop), was a solitary affair. It may not sound it – it’s made up of strong, purposeful arrangements with a huge host of musicians; filled with cradling space and warm light. This will also come as a surprise to anyone who has seen Naima perform in the time since the release of her 2022 debut Giant Palm, undoubtedly a communal experience.

With a band of ten, three, or even just solo, when Naima plays there’s a rare bond between the musicians on stage and the audience. In their interview with her, The Quietus declared “after every song the applause and cheering is immense, so immense in fact that it seems to becoming from a different place than the usual formalities of a live show, a link between performer and artist forged somewhere deeper and more personal.”

It was in Giant Palm’s music too, a record that sweeps and swells, a chorus of voices and instrumentation that rises and falls as one alongside Naima’s own somersaulting voice.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Shovel Dance Collective + Naima Bock

title: LAURIE ANDERSON: FRIENDS AND TEACHERS
description:
A special performance of portraits from her book-in-progress.

Laurie Anderson is one of the most influential and innovative artists of the past four decades. A writer, director, composer, visual artist, musician and vocalist, she has consistently pushed creative boundaries since the release of her breakthrough work, O Superman, in 1981.

Her extraordinary career has spanned music, performance, film, visual art and technology, with work presented at leading museums, theatres and institutions around the world, including Harvard University and NASA. A Grammy-winning artist and recipient of the Recording Academy’s Lifetime Achievement Award, Anderson has collaborated with a remarkable range of creative figures, including Brian Eno, Philip Glass and her life partner as well as collaborator, Lou Reed.

Making her first-ever appearance in Wales as part of Llais 2026, Anderson presents Friends and Teachers – a special performance of portraits drawn from her book-in-progress. Blending storytelling, wit and insight, this bespoke event offers a rare opportunity to experience new work from one of contemporary culture’s most distinctive voices.

Thought-provoking, intimate and deeply human, Friends and Teachers invites audiences into Anderson’s world through reflections on the people, ideas and encounters that have shaped her life and art. Expect an unforgettable evening from a pioneering artist whose work continues to inspire audiences across the globe.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Laurie Anderson: Friends and Teachers

title: BESS ATWELL
description:
Bess Atwell released her debut album Hold Your Mind at just 19, introducing a songwriter of rare emotional precision. In the years since, she has continued to grow as both a touring artist and writer, releasing two further critically acclaimed albums: Already Always and Light Sleeper.

Following the release of Already Always in late 2021, Bess toured extensively, opening for artists as varied as The National, Ben Howard, and Ed Sheeran. During this time, the digital world embraced songs such as ‘Time Comes in Roses’ and ‘Nobody’, while BBC 6 Music favourite ‘Co-op’ helped build a growing and devoted audience.

Her third album, Light Sleeper, was produced by Aaron Dessner - known for his work with Taylor Swift and as a key member of The National, a band Bess has long admired. Recorded at Long Pond Studio, the album was well received and praised by critics. Bess supported Light Sleeper with tours across the UK and Europe, while also performing her first shows in Australia and Canada. Her biggest London headline show to date took place at KOKO, followed by a debut appearance at Glastonbury Festival.

At the beginning of 2026, Bess spent most of January in Los Angeles recording her fourth studio album, set for release later this year. She then embarked on a UK and European tour with Australian band The Paper Kites.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Bess Atwell

title: BLIND BOYS OF ALABAMA + LONDON AFRICAN GOSPEL CHOIR
description:
The Blind Boys of Alabama bring a night of gospel and soul to Llais 2026 alongside London African Gospel Choir who will be performing Paul Simon’s Graceland.

The Blind Boys of Alabama are living legends of gospel music, bringing over 70 years of soul, passion, and powerful storytelling to stages around the world. Honoured with Lifetime Achievement Awards from both the National Endowment for the Arts and the GRAMMYs, inducted into the Gospel Music Hall of Fame, and winners of six GRAMMY® Awards, their extraordinary journey is a testament to resilience, artistry, and enduring spirit.

From their early days performing for pocket change in the Jim Crow South to soundtracking the Civil Rights Movement and performing for three U.S. presidents, their music carries a rich history of perseverance and hope. Their latest album, Echoes of the South, continues this legacy—earning a GRAMMY® Award and multiple nominations—offering a moving reflection on struggle, strength, and triumph.

Their story now extends beyond the stage with the release of Spirit of the South, an intimate and inspiring look into the lives, voices, and untold stories behind one of gospel’s most influential groups.

Joining them are the London African Gospel Choir, back with their critically acclaimed, soul-stirring reimagining of Paul Simon’s legendary album Graceland — marking 40 years of this timeless classic.

Performed with passion, soul, and electrifying rhythm, this concert brings together soaring voices, vibrant harmonies, and an irresistible celebration of African musical heritage.

An unforgettable night of joyful spirit and cultural fusion, the London African Gospel Choir breathes new life into classics like “You Can Call Me Al” and “Diamonds on the Soles of Her Shoes.” Whether you’re a longtime fan of the original album or discovering its magic for the first time, this is a live experience that connects generations and transcends borders.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Blind Boys of Alabama + London African Gospel Choir

title: LANDLESS
description:
Landless are: Lily Power, Méabh Meir, Ruth Clinton and Sinéad Lynch.

The Irish quartet sings centuries old ballads as well as more recently penned folk songs. Sometimes unaccompanied and at times with subtle instrumentation, their vocally rich music is dark and patient; spellbinding and gorgeous. Lúireach is their second album and as with their acclaimed debut Bleaching Bones (2018), it is produced by John ‘Spud’ Murphy, known for his work with artists such as Lankum and ØXN.

Folk music emerging from Dublin seems to be everywhere at the moment – demonstrated most clearly by Lankum gaining a host of ‘Album of the Year’ nods at the end of 2023 – but it would be a mistake to call this a movement, much less any kind of revival. While Lankum, John Francis Flynn, Ye Vagabonds, Lisa O’Neill et al might be new to a lot of audiences, these artists have been exploring and expanding what folk music can be for years, decades even. And this is just as true of Landless, the quartet who’ve been singing together since 2013, finding each other through the traditional singing scene in the city and, crucially, the Sacred Harp singing community.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Landless

title: JORDAN PLAYFAIR
description:
Jordan Playfair is a guitarist, lyricist, and composer whose work blends elements of folk, metal, and blues. His current focus is on exploring the textural possibilities of the guitar within the structure of a song.

In 2024 Jordan released his debut album ‘Something Inside So Wrong’ on the Danish label 15 Love. Written between 2013 and 2024, the album features a collection of home-recorded compositions drawn from his archive, utilising guitar, electronics, and voice.

Last year, Jordan released new music with London label AD 93.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Jordan Playfair

title: SIRENS: HOSTED BY LISA HANNIGAN
description:
An extraordinary gathering of voices for one special night.

Sirens is a new live music experience curated and hosted by Lisa Hannigan, bringing together an evolving ensemble of extraordinary female voices from across Ireland and internationally. Developed through Sounds from a Safe Harbour, the project draws inspiration from mythology, harmony, collective singing, and the transformative power of voice as a shared human experience.

With musical direction and arrangements by Theo Byrne, Sirens moves between intimate acoustic performance, layered vocal experimentation, reimagined songs, and collaborative interpretation. Each presentation features a unique constellation of artists responding to place, audience and atmosphere, creating a performance that is both immersive and unrepeatable.

Following its acclaimed debut at Sounds from a Safe Harbour, Sirens will tour Ireland and the UK in Autumn 2026 with performances in Inis Oírr, Dublin, Cork, Cardiff and London, featuring artists including Lisa Hannigan, Theodora Byrne Trio, Jane Patterson, Helen Murray, Amanda Bergman, Kate Stables, Landless, Bess Atwell, Charlotte Church and more.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Sirens: Hosted by Lisa Hannigan

title: TOMOS WILLIAMS' CWMWL TYSTION III / EMPATHY
description:
Welsh trumpeter Tomos Williams, returns to Llais with the third and final iteration of his extraordinary 'Cwmwl Tystion' project, which explores events in Welsh history through music.

Following Cwmwl Tystion II / Riot!'s performance at Llais in 2023, Tomos has once again assembled an incredible band of Welsh and international talent for Cwmwl Tystion III / Empathy.

Nia Lynn and Eadyth Crawford are two of Wales' most creative  and versatile Welsh language vocalists.

Melvin Gibbs, from Brooklyn, New York is an internationally recognised giant on the electric bass, and has been called 'The greatest bassist in the world' by Time Out New York, whose worked with everyone from Ornette Coleman to Henry Rollins, while Irish guitarist Chris Guilfoyle has established himself as one of the hottest musicians coming out of the Emerald isle.

Finally Mark O'Connor is in the drum seat alongside live visuals from Simon Proffitt, both longtime collaborators in the 'Cwmwl Tystion' project.

Cwmwl Tystion III / Empathy toured Wales in 2024, and this will be a final, exclusive, one off performance by the band at Llais – to round off the project in style, and also to celebrate the release of the album Cwmwl Tystion III / Empathy earlier this year.

The name 'Cwmwl Tystion' (cloud of witnesses) is derived from a poem by the great Welsh poet Waldo Williams and the music incorporating elements of jazz, heavy rock, and Welsh folk music augmented by live visuals will reference and commemorate events in Welsh history such as the Welsh Not, the Aberfan disaster, the Miners' Strike and Paul Robesons' long association with Wales.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Tomos Williams' Cwmwl Tystion III / Empathy

title: TRISTWCH Y FENYWOD + JOANNE ROBERTSON + JASPER LLEWELLYN
description:
A triple bill featuring some of the best experimental musicians in the UK.

Tristwch Y Fenywod is a band of three queer women who play avant garde Gothic rock using folk, rock, and digital instruments, with lyrics sung entirely in the Welsh language (Cymraeg). Sapphic love and desire, existential darkness, political and environmental anguish/celebration, psychogeographic romance, pagan mysticism, imaginal explorations of Celtic history and myth, psychedelia, and myriad other variations of reverie are conjured through the music of Tristwch Y Fenywod. They were formed in 2022 in Leeds, which is where the band is primarily based.

Joanne Robertson is a musician and painter. She collaborates regularly with friends, most recently with Dean Blunt on Backstage Raver and Sidsel Meineche Hansen on Alien Baby.

Both her painting and music emerge from improvisatory moments of expression, and her critically acclaimed album Blurrr, released via AD 93 in 2025, was written between painting sessions and while raising a child. Loose and playful in its intuition, Robertson’s vocals and guitar drift, murmur, and whisper across the record, fostering a deep intimacy as unknown emotions rise up from the well.

Jasper Llewellyn is a founding member of the band 'caroline'. He is now playing his first shows under his own name.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Tristwch y Fenywod + Joanne Robertson + Jasper Llewellyn

title: BUENA VISTA ALL STARS + ORCHESTRA BAOBAB
description:
Immerse yourself in a spectacular double bill celebrating the musical connections between Cuba and West Africa, performed by two of the world’s most exciting and influential ensembles.

Buena Vista All Stars are a legendary orchestra filled with the best Cuban musicians whose vibrant performances have captivated audiences across the globe. Blending traditional Cuban rhythms with African and Spanish influences, the ensemble brings the beauty, passion and spirit of Cuba to life through masterful musicianship and infectious energy.

Rooted in generations of musical heritage while embracing a fresh and contemporary spirit, Buena Vista All Stars honour the enduring legacy of Cuban music while celebrating its place as a living, evolving art form.

Joining them on the bill, Orchestra Baobab will bring the sounds of Senegal to Cardiff. Founded in Dakar in 1970, the celebrated group became a cornerstone of African music with its distinctive fusion of Afro-Cuban rhythms, Wolof, Mandinka and Serer musical traditions.

Constantly reinventing their sound while remaining true to their roots, Orchestra Baobab have captivated audiences for decades with their hypnotic grooves, elegant melodies and exceptional musicianship. From the intimate clubs of Dakar to stages around the world, their music tells the story of a rich and diverse cultural heritage.

Together, these two iconic ensembles invite you on an unforgettable musical journey filled with rhythm, tradition and timeless songs that transcend borders and connect cultures.

title: ABERFAN 60
description:
REMEMBRANCE · COMMUNITY · HOPE

Marking the 60 years since the Aberfan disaster, this concert is anchored by Paul Mealor’s newly commissioned From Darkness into Light: a concert requiem for hope, bringing together Mark Lewis Jones, Aberfan Schools Choirs, Ynysowen Male Voice Choir, and the BBC National Chorus of Wales in an act of remembrance. Framing this centrepiece is music that moves from urgency to hope: Anna Clyne’s This Moment flashes with restless energy; Haydn’s E minor “Mourning” Symphony (No. 44) drives forward with fierce intensity; Mozart offers weight and luminous calm in the Andante cantabile from the “Jupiter”; and Vaughan Williams’ Whitman-inspired Toward the Unknown Region sets out on a searching journey towards the horizon.

title: FRAMERATE: PULSE OF THE EARTH
description:
FRAMERATE: Pulse of the Earth’s hypnotic imagery bears witness to landscapes in flux. The impact of human behaviour and the immense force of nature unfolds around you across an array of screens. This is a space where your perspective may shift.

FRAMERATE: Pulse of the Earth is the first in the FRAMERATE series. The work reveals alterations caused by human-centred industry and the rhythms of the natural world; destruction, extraction, habitation, construction, harvests, growth, and erosion. Three-dimensional stories unfold across this multichannel installation. Hypnotic imagery surrounds you. Audio shifts through the space. Spring breaks, summer sun shines through the leaves as they turn amber and fall a second later. In a quaint English garden a pumpkin grows. A thousand tonnes of steel are crushed. Sand ebbs and flows while a cliff retreats. 268 cows are milked. 519 pints are drunk.

Created from thousands of daily 3D time-lapse scans of British landscapes, the work observes change on a scale impossible to see with the lens of traditional cameras.

This is not just an artwork. The data collected and presented by FRAMERATE is ground-breaking scientific research, containing empirical, measurable facts published that have since been published in NATURE.

"FRAMERATE: Pulse of the Earth manifests as art, meditation and science in concert. Our team 3D time-lapse recorded urban, rural and industrial sites changing over time. The resulting hypnotic imagery observes environmental change on a spatial and temporal scale. With these ground- breaking visuals, we have created a unique installation guided by principles of architecture, theatre, music and mindfulness. This work invites people to consider their relationships to time, the environment, their community, and to change—offering a new way of looking at the world and relating to the planet." - Director's Statement.

title: PHILIP CLOUTS QUARTET
description:
Melodic jazz with inspirations from around the world.

Cape Town-born pianist/composer Clouts’ South African roots have inspired a voyage of discovery that has led to him soaking up the joyful passion of Caribbean calypso, the bluesy melodies of Middle Eastern praise songs, the exuberant sway of Cuban dance music and the tuneful essence of Gospel while honouring jazz heroes including Bill Evans, Keith Jarrett and Charles Lloyd.

As a key member of the popular London-based world jazz ensemble Zubop and its offshoot ZubopGambia, with BBC World Music Award-winner Juldeh Camara, Clouts created a solid body of work with African roots and, since moving to Dorset in 2006, he has responded to his new surroundings with impressionistic compositions that complement his world music interests, resonating with strong themes and packing a mighty rhythmical punch.

The latest CD from the Philip Clouts Quartet is one of the first wave of releases on the new jazz imprint from prestigious label Odradek Records. On this album, entitled Umoya (named from the Zulu word for life force), Clouts’ African inspirations extend beyond Cape jazz to Gnawa music and Afrobeat, and further to pan-European folksong and soul-jazz.

Joined by rising star saxophonist Samuel Eagles, bassist Tim Fairhall and drummer Ted Carrasco, he brings his musical journey alive with superb musicianship and infectious vigour.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Philip Clouts Quartet

description:

In 1400, Owain Glyndŵr (Michael Sheen), a forgotten lord of a small northern land, is declared an outlaw by King Henry IV (Linus Roache). Rather than surrendering to his fate, Owain rises in rebellion. As the spark of his revolt spreads across the border, Henry finds himself struggling to keep the throne and the two men find themselves on opposite sides of history; one fighting for survival, the other for control.

Written by Olivier Award-winning Welsh playwright Gary Owen (Iphigenia in Splott), Owain & Henry is an historical epic charged with poetic power. This ambitious new production brings to life one of Wales’ most defining stories, where the fight for the existence of a nation hangs in the balance.

Co-directed by Michael Sheen and Steffan Donnelly of Theatr Cymru.

title: WAR AND PEACE
description:
ELEGY JOURNEY RESILIENCE

War and peace meet in music of remembrance, journeying, and hardwon joy. Ravel opens with Le Tombeau de Couperin, his 1917 suite reimagined for orchestra: Baroque dance forms refracted through glittering colour, sudden shifts of light and delicately layered sound.  Vaughan Williams then turns inward with Songs of Travel, sung here by baritone Steffan Lloyd Owen, tales of the wanderer shaped by folk song and hymn-like warmth. The journey then turns north with Sibelius’s Symphony No. 1 in E minor, a work that announces the arrival of a distinctive symphonic voice. Premiered in 1899, its brooding clarinet opening leads without pause into bold drama, while striking string and woodwind solos shape music alive with urgency and sweep. Though echoes of Tchaikovsky’s lyricism and Romantic intensity, the symphony speaks with unmistakable individuality, culminating in a hammering scherzo and a finale of stirring force.

7Steps perform some of the classics associated with the great trumpeter; So What, All Blues, Milestones but also play some of the less well known songs from Miles' vast catalogue such as Joshua, Masqualero and Teo.

2026 is the centenary year of Miles Davis' birth, and 7Steps will perform the music of one of the towering figures of 20th Century music, with passion and vigour.

The quintet, includes stellar Welsh jazz musicians Joe Northwood on tenor sax, pianist Dave Jones, Welsh jazz royalty Paula Gardiner on bass and the magnificent Mark O'Connor on drums.

Tomos Williams is a leading and unique voice on the Welsh jazz scene. Heavily indebted and influenced by Miles' music ,7Steps is a natural project for Tomos to front. Tomos also leads the jazz/folk sextet, Burum, the groundbreaking Indo-Welsh fusion band 'Khamira',  and his Cwmwl Tystion/Witness project.

HK Gruber’s Short Stories from the Vienna Woods opens the evening with a series of sharply characterised musical illustrations, by turns playful, ironic and darkly expressive.At the heart of the concert is the world premiere of Erika Fox’s Viola Concerto, performed by celebrated soloist Lawrence Power. Richly exploratory in colour and gesture, the concerto places the viola centre stage, showcasing its expressive depth through Fox’s distinctive blend of lyricism and energetic drive.Finally, we have the UK premiere of Steven Mackey’s Concerto for Curved Space. A virtuosic and kaleidoscopic journey, the work bends rhythm, harmony and genre with irrepressible momentum, drawing the evening to a thrilling and expansive close.

description:
Join us at MAMMA MIA! and enjoy the ultimate feel-good factor at the world’s sunniest and most exhilarating smash-hit musical in Cardiff from 30 November 2026 for one week only!

Set on a Greek island paradise, a story of love, friendship and identity is cleverly told through the timeless songs of ABBA.

Sophie’s quest to discover the father she’s never known brings her mother face to face with three men from her distant romantic past on the eve of a wedding they’ll never forget.

This irresistibly funny show has been thrilling audiences all around the world and now there’s never been a better time to see this unforgettable musical in Cardiff.

Whatever age you are, you can’t help but have the time of your life at MAMMA MIA!

title: TCHAIKOVSKY’S NUTCRACKER
description:
MAGIC WONDER DELIGHTFUL

A festive, family friendly celebration of Seasonal classics, conducted by Luis Castillo Briceño. The evening opens with the magical Prelude from Humperdinck’s Hänsel und Gretel, where folk inspired melodies and glowing orchestral colours bring the fairy tale forest vividly to life. Frank Bridge’s sparkling Christmas Dance “Sir Roger de Coverley” follows, a whirlwind of variations on a much loved English tune traditionally played at Christmas celebrations, ending with a joyful nod to Auld Lang Syne.Benjamin Britten’s much loved Young Person’s Guide to the Orchestra offers an entertaining and illuminating tour of the orchestra, perfect for curious listeners of all ages. After the interval, Tchaikovsky’s irresistible Nutcracker Suite brings the concert to a close, overflowing with seasonal magic, dance, and unforgettable melodies.

Artists:

Luis Castillo-Briceno – Conductor

Steffan Rhodri – Narrator

Repertoire:

Humperdinck Hänsel und Gretel: Prelude Bridge Christmas Dance ""Sir Roger de Coverley"" Britten Young Person's Guide to the Orchestra INTERVAL Tchaikovsky Suite from Nutcracker

title: CAMILLE O'SULLIVAN - LOVELETTER
description:
A love letter in song, Camille’s celebrates dear friend Shane MacGowan, Sinéad O’Connor, David Bowie, Radiohead, Brel, Nick Cave and more. Chameleon-like on stage, each song has a different character with its story to tell.

Camille with long-time collaborator Feargal Murray has created an intimate, heartfelt show with a little bit of joyful, mad chaos as her life unravels, capturing the honest response to those much loved and lost.

Voted “One of the top 25 performances ever on Later with Jools BBC” (Daily Telegraph) and "Queen of the Edinburgh Festival" (BBC), Camille toured with the Pogues, guested at Yoko Ono’s & Richard Thompson’s RFH Meltdown and original star of Olivier Award-winning La Clique. Previously an award-winning architect and painter, Camille was born in London to a French mother and Irish/English father, she grew up in a village in Cork, Ireland listening to her parents & sisters eclectic music collection that shaped her into the unique interpreter she is today.

The multi-award-winning singer has stunned audiences around the world with her five-star sell-out performances, including the Sydney Opera House, Royal Festival Hall, The Roundhouse, won the coveted Herald Angel award for her RSC solo performance ‘The Rape of Lucrece’ and recently an Architectural RIAI 2025 award.

Dark, sexy, fierce, amusing and mesmerizing, Camille transforms each song she performs into an intense, emotional, and theatrical experience. Expect joy and pure passion.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Camille O'Sullivan - Loveletter

title: LEROY BRITO - HALFTIME
description:
As seen on Netflix's smash hit Baby Reindeer, with tour support slots for Rhod Gilbert and Mo Gilligan, Leroy Brito is back with his biggest and most ambitious show to date.

Halftime is Leroy's hilarious new hour of stand-up about turning 45, accepting that you're officially middle-aged, and stepping into your DILF era.

title: MATILDA THE MUSICAL
description:
Following the sellout success of its first tour in 2018/19, Matilda The Musical, the multi-award winning musical from the Royal Shakespeare Company, inspired by the beloved book by Roald Dahl, is heading back out on tour across the UK and Ireland.

In celebration of 15 years on stage since opening at the Courtyard Theatre in Stratford-upon-Avon, and following performances in 100 cities across 17 countries worldwide, Matilda now returns to Wales Millennium Centre.

With book by Dennis Kelly, music and lyrics by Tim Minchin and directed by Matthew Warchus, Matilda is the story of an extraordinary little girl who, armed with a vivid imagination and a sharp mind, dares to take a stand and change her own destiny.

Winner of over 100 international awards, including 24 for Best Musical, the ‘unique and unforgettable’ (Rolling Stone) global phenomenon, Matilda has now delighted over 12 million audiences worldwide.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Matilda The Musical

title: BARRYLESQUE
description:
Hold on to your paper hats and fizz... This Christmas, Wales Millennium Centre is bringing you the most glamorous, most outrageous and most unmissably Welsh night out of the festive season.

Barrylesque is a drag cabaret spectacular that takes the beloved world of Gavin & Stacey and gives it the full Barry Island treatment. Featuring all your fave characters, reimagined as larger-than-life drag and burlesque performers for a night of live vocals, lip sync, comedy and chaos. Expect iconic catchphrases, outrageous characters, and a singalong finale that'll have the whole house on its feet. Tidy.

And maybe, just maybe, we might finally work out what happened on that fishing trip.

Part cabaret, part sitcom, entirely tongue-in-cheek, Barrylesque is the only Christmas gift worth giving this year.

Don't miss it. It's well lush.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2026 > Barrylesque

title: THE MAGIC OF CHRISTMAS
description:
Celebrate the season with an uplifting evening of music as we bring you our Christmas Celebration concerts, filled with warmth, joy, and sparkle.

This festive programme brings together much‑loved seasonal favourites alongside orchestral showpieces that capture the magic of Christmas.

Perfect for families, friends, and all who enjoy marking Christmas through music, this concert offers a chance to pause, reflect, and rejoice.

Join us for an evening of festive cheer, heartfelt music, and the shared spirit of Christmas.

title: TCHAIKOVSKY 5
description:
This richly coloured concert is conducted by Principal Guest Conductor Jaime Martín and brings together music of atmosphere, virtuosity and symphonic power.

Grace Williams’ Sea Sketches opens the evening, capturing the character of the Welsh coastline in music of freshness, colour and flowing movement.

The focus then turns to harpist Mared Pugh‑Evans, soloist in Henriette Renié’s Harp Concerto, a deeply Romantic work shaped by long, sweeping melodies and brilliant, virtuosic passages for the harp.

After the interval, Tchaikovsky’s Symphony No. 5 charts a dramatic journey from struggle to hard‑won triumph, bringing the programme to an impassioned close.

Expressive Rich Destiny

Williams Sea Sketches (20')Henreitte Renie Harp Concerto (25')Interval Tchaikovsky Symphony No.5 (44')
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2027 > Tchaikovsky 5

title: STRAUSS & WAGNER
description:
Strauss & Wagner: two towering figures at the height of their expressive powers.

Richard Strauss’s Four Last Songs, composed in 1948, a year before his death, stand as one of the most luminous farewells in all music. Setting deeply contemplative texts, Strauss reflects on love, transience and release, drawing the listener into what he called “the magic circle of the night.”

After the interval, Wagner’s Tristan und Isolde: An Orchestral Passion reveals the composer at his most revolutionary. This sumptuous orchestral synthesis has long been cherished as a concert work in its own right, its lush romantic surface concealing a daring harmonic language that transformed music history from its opening bars.

Conducted by Anthony Hermus, the programme offers an immersive journey through two composers redefining the emotional and musical possibilities of their art.

PASSION FAREWELL LUMINOUS Strauss VIER LETZTE LIEDER (Four Last Songs) (24') Interval (20') Wagner arr. | trefn. Henk de Vlieger Tristan und Isolde: An Orchestral Passion (60')

title: PARANORMAL ACTIVITY
description:
The sell-out West End & International phenomenon, direct from London with brand-new special effects.

James and Lou move from Chicago to London to escape their past, but they soon discover that places aren’t haunted, people are...

Inspired by the iconic, terrifying film series, Paranormal Activity is a new story live on stage.

The spine-chilling production stars James Bye (2:22: A Ghost Story, EastEnders) as James, Hannah Sinclair Robinson (The Play That Goes Wrong, The Curious Incident of the Dog in the Night-Time) as Lou, Jo Castleton (War Horse) as Etheline Cotgrave and Caroline Faber (Network, The Heiress) as Carolanne.

Now embarking on its first ever UK and Ireland tour after a sell-out, extended run in London, thisthrilling production promises to keep you on the edge of your seat from start to finish.

Hold your nerve...

title: CITIES OF SOUND: NEW YORK, BERLIN, VIENNA
description:
From Mozart’s classical brilliance to the bold energy of twentieth century modernism, this programme crackles with theatrical flair and rhythmic drive.

Conductor Anna Rakitina leads a richly varied evening that opens with a suite from Elena Langer’s Figaro Gets a Divorce, a witty and expressive sequel to Mozart’s operatic world. Mozart himself follows with the radiant Piano Concerto No. 21, its elegance and lyrical warmth brought to life by pianist Clare Hammond.

After the interval, George Antheil’s Jazz Symphony bursts with swagger and rhythmic bite, before Stravinsky’s Symphony in Three Movements delivers a bracing, propulsive finale.

BRILLIANCE THEATRE RHYTHM

Elena Langer Figaro Gets a Divorce  (20') Mozart Piano Concerto No.21  (26') Interval George Anthiel Jazz Symphony  Stravinsky Symphony in Three Movements  (22')
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2027 > Cities of Sound: New York, Berlin, Vienna

title: IT'S MY SHOUT AWARDS
description:
One of the biggest nights in the Welsh creative calendar is back. The It’s My Shout Awards is returning to Wales Millennium Centre in January, to shine a spotlight on the finest emerging filmmaking talent coming out of Wales.

Join us for a spectacular televised event packed with glitz, glamour, and a star-studded red carpet. This evening celebrates a phenomenal year of broadcast content produced by It's My Shout, bringing together special guests from the screen, stage, and online worlds.

Why you can't miss it:

Don't miss your chance to be part of the magic.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2027 > It's My Shout Awards

title: THE FULL MONTY
description:
Sometimes you have to bare everything!

Celebrating the 30th Anniversary of the iconic film that took British cinema by storm, The Everyman Theatre, Cheltenham and Buxton Opera House in association with Mark Goucher and David Pugh present The Full Monty, live on stage. Back by popular demand, the boys are returning with a major national tour!

There are no heroes in Simon Beaufoy’s heartfelt play, just a group of lads trying to regain their dignity and pride. This fast and funny play is still very much of our time, as again we are hit by a cost-of-living crisis. Gaz and his mates are down on their luck and feel they have been thrown on the scrap heap, but they are determined to fight back and bare a little more than they ever thought they would have to.

As in the 1997 smash hit film, this production is a rollercoaster ride of ups and downs, laughs and heartbreak. Book now to relive the music of the 90’s and have a great night out in the company of our group of lads as they work to put on the show of their lives.

Starring Kevin Clifton (Strictly Come Dancing, Priscilla Queen of the Desert UK & Ireland Tour 2026) as Gaz, Stewart Wright (Doc Martin, The Upstart Crow–Apollo Theatre) as Dave, James Gaddas (Coronation Street, The Rocky Horror Picture Show UK Tour) as Gerald, Ben Onwukwe (The Full Monty UK Tour 2024, The Shawshank Redemption UK Tour) as Horse, Jon-Paul Bell (Hollyoaks, Masters of Air) as Guy and Zrey Sholapurkar (Lark Rise to Candleford–The Watermill Theatre, The History Boys UK Tour) as Lomper.

title: CLASSICAL WIND DOWN LIVE WITH NIALL BRESLIN
description:
Join us for Classical Wind Down LIVE, an hour of calming classical music to help you release the stresses of the day, recharge and prepare to rest - presented by Irish musician and mindfulness expert Niall Breslin.

CALM RESTORE BALANCE

Rosey Chan Adagio for Planet Earth (4’) Judith Weir Still, Glowing (3’)  Delius North Country Sketches: Autumn, The Wind Soughs in the Trees (8’) Dvorak Silent Woods (for Solo Cello and Orchestra (6’) Rautavaara Mvmt 2 "Melankolia" from Cantus Arcticus "Concerto for Birds and Orchestra” (5') Ravel Une barque sur l'océan (7’) Howard Skempton Lento (13’)

title: IN TIMES OF WAR
description:
Under the baton of Jörg Widmann, this fascinating programme journeys from jubilant celebration to an urgent plea for peace.

Schumann’s Symphony No. 3, opens the evening with an exuberant tribute to the Rhine, its leaping, syncopated themes surging with life and purpose. Heroic horn calls shape the symphony’s noble character, giving centre stage to the majestic fourth movement, inspired by the solemn grandeur of an archbishop’s elevation to cardinal.

After the interval, Widmann’s own Cantata in tempore belli (Cantata in Times of War) delivers a powerful, searing response to conflict. Featuring Jess Dandy and narrator Amira Casar, the work weaves biblical texts, poetry and Wolfgang Borchert’s uncompromising pacifist appeal, “Say No!”, into an unforgettable statement against war and in hope for peace.

NOBILITY PROTEST RESOLVE

Schumann Symphony No.3 (32') Interval Jorg Widmann Cantata in tempore belli (Cantata in Times of War) (45')
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2027 > In Times of War

title: DAN & PHIL
description:
Dan & Phil: Hard Launch World Tour

Dan and Phil finally hard launched and are crash landing in a city near you. In this unhinged and unafraid new era, join Dan and Phil live with their explosive new stage show for a much-needed night of outrageous oversharing, scream-laughing, and celebrating that we're all still here and we made it.

This show is for everyone - from casual male-podcast listeners, to friends & fam that lost bets, and the people that have been here since the beginning! Grab a ticket and don't miss out on the memories ..as they might never leave the house together again.

title: BLOOD BROTHERS
description:
Written by Willy Russell, the legendary BLOOD BROTHERS tells the captivating and moving tale of twins who, separated at birth, grow up on opposite sides of the tracks, only to meet again with fateful consequences.

Few musicals have received quite such acclaim as the multi-award-winning BLOOD BROTHERS. The production ran for more than 10,000 performances in London’s West End and has been affectionately christened the ‘Standing Ovation Musical’ as inevitably it “brings the audience cheering to its feet and roaring its approval” (The Daily Mail).

The superb score includes Bright New Day, Marilyn Monroe and the emotionally charged hit Tell Me It’s Not True.

title: ANDREW BIRD - ON THE EDGE TOUR
description:
Back with a brand-new show, Andrew has just supported Russell Howard on his current national tour including four straight shows at The London Palladium. He has also recently supported Rhod Gilbert and Troy Hawke and at The UK Comedy Awards 2023 was voted Comic’s Comic-Best Act.

Andrew is always worried or stressed about something. From global events to finding free parking. From a wife hitting the perimenopause combined with two teenage kids, to hanging a wine-rack. How can he not be “on edge”

Having previously supported Russell at Bristol's Ashton Gate Football stadium he’s also supported Rob Brydon, America’s Brian Regan and Michelle Wolfe on their only London shows and Michael McIntyre on an entire arena tour including Wembley and the O2.

He was only 1 of 7 comedians to perform in front of Banksy at Dismal Land and he’s written on the recent series of 8 Out of 10 Cats Does Countdown.

title: CHICAGO
description:
CHICAGO, the "sexiest musical ever" (Metro) is back on Tour in 2027.

“Murder, greed, corruption, exploitation, adultery and treachery…all those things we hold near and dear to our hearts”. So begins the international multi-award-winning musical, CHICAGO.

Set amidst the razzle-dazzle decadence of the 1920s, CHICAGO is the story of Roxie Hart, a housewife and nightclub dancer who murders her on-the-side lover after he threatens to walk out on her. Desperate to avoid conviction, she dupes the public, the media and her rival cellmate, Velma Kelly, by hiring Chicago’s slickest criminal lawyer to transform her malicious crime into a barrage of sensational headlines, the likes of which might just as easily be ripped from today's tabloids.

Created by the musical theatre talents of John Kander, Fred Ebb and legendary choreographer Bob Fosse, CHICAGO’s sexy, sassy score with one show-stopping song after another includes “Razzle Dazzle”, “Cell Block Tango”, and “All That Jazz”. With 6 Tony Awards, 2 Olivier Awards, a Grammy® and thousands of standing ovations, CHICAGO truly is “SUPERB” (Daily Telegraph).

Don't miss out, book now! It would be criminal to miss it...

*Cast and performance schedule subject to change without notice.

title: SIBELIUS 6 & 7
description:
This programme traces a journey from Romantic drama to Nordic quality under the baton of Pietari Inkinen, with Anna Geniushine as soloist.

Wagner’s Overture to Tannhäuser opens the concert with a powerful depiction of inner conflict. As Wagner described it, the overture stands as a complete musical argument in itself, from the solemn tread of the Pilgrims’ Chorus to the intoxicating swirl of the Venusberg.

Grieg’s Piano Concerto in A minor follows, a work of rhapsodic imagination and vivid colour. Tender lyricism alternates with dazzling virtuosity, evoking Nordic landscapes and mythical figures.

After the interval, Sibelius’s Sixth and Seventh Symphonies offer a vision of symphonic form reimagined. These distilled, continuous works unfold as profound emotional statements, culminating in the transcendent power of the Seventh Symphony.

CONFLICT MYTH STILLNESS

Wagner Tannhäuser Overture (14') Grieg Piano Concerto (30') Interval (20') Sibelius Symphony No.6  (28') Sibelius Symphony No.7 (21')
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2027 > Sibelius 6 & 7

title: ROB AUTON 'JUPITER'
description:
This show is a story about a time when Rob Auton had a job as an estate agent on the planet Jupiter.

It is fiction. Following the success of his sell-out 2025-26 nationwide tour, multi-award-winning writer, performer, podcaster and actor Rob Auton is returning to stages across the UK in 2027 with his thirteenth hour JUPITER.

On screen Rob has appeared opposite Danny Dyer in Marching Powder, in Channel 4's hit comedy The Change, and in BBC's Starstruck, with further credits including Miracle Workers (TBS), The End of the F**ing World (Netflix/Channel 4), The Russell Howard Hour (Sky), Cold Feet (ITV) and Random Acts (Channel 4). His viral stand-up appearance on Stand-Up Central with Rob Delaney (Comedy Central)

Alongside his screen work, Rob is a two-time British Podcast Awards Gold winner for The Rob Auton Daily Podcast.
subcategory: Wales Millennium Centre > What's on > 2027 > Rob Auton  'JUPITER'

title: JESUS CHRIST SUPERSTAR
description:
CARDIFF, WHAT’S THE BUZZ?

The record-breaking West End production of Jesus Christ Superstar, starring Sam Ryder in the iconic role of Jesus is now coming to Wales Millennium Centre for 2 weeks only.

Tim Rice and Andrew Lloyd Webber’s Jesus Christ Superstar follows the events of the last days of the life of Jesus Christ, as seen through the eyes of Judas. Reflecting the rock roots that defined a generation, the legendary score includes ‘I Don’t Know How to Love Him’, ‘Gethsemane’ and the iconic title number ‘Superstar’.

Tim Sheader directs the global phenomenon, with choreography by Olivier Award-winner Drew McOnie and design by Tony and Olivier Award-winner Tom Scutt.

title: WELSH NATIONAL OPERA: THE ANONYMOUS LOVER
description:
Playful, witty and irresistibly charming, The Anonymous Lover is a sparkling romantic comedy about the risks and rewards of falling in love.

Léontine, a wealthy widow, swears she’ll never love again after an unhappy marriage. When mysterious letters and thoughtful gifts begin arriving from a secret admirer, her resolve starts to waver. The sender is her friend Valcour, who hides his identity, fearing rejection because of his lower social standing. As Léontine searches for the truth, Valcour must decide whether to reveal himself or remain anonymous.

Rarely performed, The Anonymous Lover is the only surviving opera by French composer Joseph Bologne and is brought to life in a vibrant new staging, with the orchestra on stage in an energetic baroque-inspired world. Faithful to Bologne’s elegant score, it also introduces a fresh, contemporary voice that speaks directly to the audience - inviting you to look again, think differently, and decide for yourself what shapes the way we experience great art.

wno.org.uk/anonlover

New text by Tife Kusoro

Conductor Frederick Brown

Musical Supervisor Laurence Cumings

Director Omar Elerian  Leontine Nardus Williams

title: FRIDAY NIGHT IS MUSIC NIGHT - MUSIC OF THE COAST
description:
SEASCAPES | ADVENTURE | ATMOSPHERE

Under the direction of David Brophy, this BBC Radio 3 Friday Night is Music Night celebrates Britain’s enduring relationship with the sea, blending light hearted charm with richly atmospheric music.

From the overture to Sullivan’s irresistible H.M.S. Pinafore to Walton’s exuberant Portsmouth Point, the first half evokes coastal life in all its colour and variety. Soloist Gareth Brynmor John brings narrative to settings of John Ireland’s Sea Fever and Rebecca Clarke’s haunting The Seal Man, while Bax’s evocative tone poem Tintagel rises in romantic splendour, its waves surging against the Cornish cliffs.

After the interval, our seafaring adventure continues with Korngold’s swashbuckling The Sea Hawk, alongside miniatures of seaside wit and nostalgia by Whitlock and Hedges. The concert culminates in Britten’s Four Sea Interludes, a timeless portrayal of the sea’s ever-changing moods.
